newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA TO HOLD TENDER SALE OF VENTSPILS ABROAD.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA TO HOLD TENDER SALE OF VENTSPILS ABROAD.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday that it will organise an tender for investment houses to sell seven percent of oil terminal group Ventspils Nafta to foreign investors.
The tender will also ask for offers to organise the previously announce sale of shares in leading bank Unibanka.

LPA legal director Viktor Shadinov said that the tender would be organised as soon as rules for the sale of the company, one of the main outlets for Russian crude oil, have been confirmed by the LPA's board.
He said this could happen in around two weeks.
"Then we will accounce an international tender for financial intermediaries to place Unibanka and Ventspils Nafta," Shadinov told Reuters.
"Nomura has already offered its services. According to the law we have to have a tender," he added.
He said the timing of the placement would depend on the group chosen to arrange the issue abroad.

The LPA earlier announced that Ventspils will be sold in four stages, with the third stage involving a public offer of 15.5 percent of the shares, five percent for cash and seven percent in an international offer.
The rules are still considered to be a working draft and have to be formally confirmed by the LPA board.
